author: i. j. carroll
title: Mary Gay Scanlon addresses WPSU closure and detention center oversight on social media - South Delco News
text:
Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon, who represents Pennsylvania’s 5th district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of statements on September 17, 2025, addressing issues ranging from local media closures to federal oversight at detention centers.
In her first post of the day, Scanlon highlighted concerns over public broadcasting services in rural Pennsylvania: “WPSU, which serves Penn State & 24 rural PA communities, will be the first NPR & PBS affiliate to shut down in the country. We are losing an organization that provides public media and emergency broadcasting capabilities to a large part of our state due to the Trump” (September 17, 2025).
Later that afternoon, she commented on national discourse around justice and social media: “The American People don’t want social media influencers to wave around binders. They want justice for the victims.” (September 17, 2025).
Scanlon also raised concerns about transparency at immigration detention facilities. She stated: “Moshannon Valley Processing Center denied me entry when I tried to conduct Congressional oversight after hearing allegations of abuse and excessive force. ICE is not going after the worst of the worst. They’ve detained people trying to follow the law, which is unacceptable.” (September 17, 2025).
Mary Gay Scanlon has served as a member of Congress since replacing Pat Meehan in 2018 and currently resides in Swarthmore. Born in Watertown, New York in 1959 and now aged 63, she holds degrees from Colgate University and earned her JD from the University of Pennsylvania.
